observations: Short one-line incidents such as disk-full, cooler failure, stale fixture and UPS loss were found by nearly every note, while events embedded in tables or experience logs were missed far more often, especially the per-row faults in the kernarg report.

The most serious verdict errors came from merging separate arms or misreading a threshold: notes A and E on the Ornith report moved the Qwen 16 t/s figure onto Ornith, D on the sharp report put +2 inside the grey zone, and D on the hardest-tasks report called a sampling best the overall best.
FACT lines were usually correct in meaning but often spent slots on context numbers such as peak VRAM or wall time, as in C, D, E and H on the sharp report and A and C on the hardest-tasks report.

Across the syntheses, Q, V, R and S caught the conflict between the stew675 ROCm recipe and the kernarg fix, while P, T, U and W did not; P and W reported no conflicts at all, and W had the widest scope.
OPEN questions were strong almost everywhere because the reports label them explicitly, so this field separated notes very little.
